cards.title: Introduction to Databases in Flask
cards.content:
Flask does not come with a built-in database layer. Instead, we use extensions like Flask-SQLAlchemy to interact with relational databases easily using an Object-Relational Mapper (ORM).

from flask_sqlalchemy import SQLAlchemy
db = SQLAlchemy(app)

options.text: Object-Relational Mapping allows interacting with the database using Python objects.
Object-Relational Mapping is a new type of database engine.
It is used exclusively to write raw SQL queries in Flask.

cards.title: Defining Database Models
cards.content:
Models in Flask-SQLAlchemy are Python classes that inherit from db.Model. Each class represents a table in the database, and attributes represent columns.

class User(db.Model):
    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    username = db.Column(db.String(80), unique=True, nullable=False)

cards.title: Performing CRUD Operations
cards.content:
CRUD stands for Create, Read, Update, and Delete. With Flask-SQLAlchemy, we use the database session to manage these operations.

# Create
new_user = User(username='alice')
db.session.add(new_user)
db.session.commit()

# Read
users = User.query.all()
